correctness.rationale: For arbitrary prime-power q=p^f and n>=1, derivations of the nonunital ideal B_n are exactly D_b(x)=x' b with b in tF_q[t]/(t^(n+1)), because D is determined by D(t) and the defining relation adds no condition. If s is the least index of an x coefficient with p not dividing s, then x' = t^(s-1)u with u(0) nonzero; hence {D_b(x)}=t^s B_full. If x'=0, every D_b(x)=0. This proves necessity of zero columns at p-multiples and columns supported in degrees >=j elsewhere, and sufficiency for every x, not merely the basis. The count of free cells gives D=sum_{p not|j}(n-j+1). Ordering eligible columns j_i descending nests each available column space U_{j_i}; with span dimension s there are q^s choices to maintain rank and q^d_i-q^s to raise it. Thus the recurrence and product are exact. The full-rank probability exponent satisfies d_i-(i-1)=1+floor(n/p)-floor(j_i/p), giving the stated residue product; the positive infinite product follows from a summable deficit. Edge cases n<p, n=p, n=1 and r=0 are encompassed. Independently authored GF(2), GF(3), and GF(4) Gaussian elimination enumerated structural matrix rank profiles (n,p,q)=(1,2,2),(3,2,2),(4,2,2),(5,2,2),(3,3,3),(4,3,3),(3,2,4),(4,2,4), including extension field F4 via a^2+a+1; all matched the recurrence and rational products. Separately, all linear maps were directly tested against all possible Leibniz derivation values for (n,q)=(2,3),(3,2),(4,2): 27,16,64 local maps respectively, matching the structural counts. These finite checks corroborate, but do not replace, the all-parameter proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For each eligible j, choose f_j=(j t^(j-1))^(-1)Delta(t^j), a polynomial divisible by t, where the inverse means division by the nonzero scalar j and monomial t^(j-1) of the known output. Then Delta is the reduction of the known sum f_j h_j; every such sum is local. For descending eligible j_i, q^(d_i) possible columns exist, q^s preserve current span of dimension s, and q^(d_i)-q^s raise rank. This proves the assigned F_s recurrence from the known Ferrers matrix census and elementary linear algebra. All-rank probability equals product_{i=1}^m(1-q^{i-1-d_i}); since d_i-(i-1)=1+floor(n/p)-floor(j_i/p), grouping by j_i residue blocks gives the stated (1-q^-1)^r prod_{h=1}^ell(1-q^{-(h+1)})^(p-1); the residue limits follow from summability. This leaves no independent new theorem in the submitted final package.

originality.rationale: The joint implication of prior primary theorems covers the asserted finite local-derivation space and all rank counts: Zielinski (2002), Theorem 8, classifies every local derivation on k[[t]] as a sum f_j h_j with h_j(x)=j[x]_{t^j}t^{j-1}. For the nonunital quotient, restrict to f_j in t k[[t]] and j<=n; this gives exactly arbitrary image columns in t^j k[t]/(t^{n+1}) when p does not divide j, with zero columns when p divides j. Conversely any finite local derivation has precisely these columns by its pointwise Leibniz-image condition, and the extension by f_j=Delta(t^j)/(j t^{j-1}) is covered by Theorem 8 and descends to the finite nilpotent quotient. The allowed matrix support is a Ferrers shape after row reversal and deletion of zero columns. Haglund's general rank-distribution theorem, reproduced as Theorem 1.9 by Cotardo-Gruica-Ravagnani (2023), already counts matrices of every rank on any such shape; the displayed recurrence, maximal-rank probability, and its residue limits are direct nested-column counting and elementary grouping. No identical displayed product was located, but matching wording/numbers is not required for mathematical coverage. The complex-only Theorem 5.1 of Abdurasulov et al. alone does not cover characteristic p. The Leibniz-algebra Resultary results concern different multiplication and are not used for this prior-implication conclusion.
residual_risks: The exact periodic maximal-rank probability appears not to be printed in the sources reviewed. This is not sufficient to establish independent originality because the calculation is a short consequence of known complete operator and Ferrers rank classifications.
The general Ferrers rank census in Cotardo et al. is reproduced from Haglund; its true earlier origin predates 2023, and no claim of new rank-enumeration technique is warranted.
Specialized finite-truncation references not indexed by the performed searches might state the exact (n,p,q) formula, which would only strengthen the rejection.

value.rationale: The algebra is natural and its characteristic-dependent rank-density statistic is meaningful as an example. But as a proposed independent discovery the exact operator space is the direct finite quotient/ideal restriction of Zielinski's complete local-derivation theorem, the full rank spectrum is an ordinary Ferrers q-rook specialization, and the displayed product/residue limits arise by one nested-subspace count and grouping factors. No new structural obstruction beyond those already encoded in h_j, distinctive unknown invariant beyond the covered specialization, or independently motivated conceptual advance is supplied. The p-periodicity is a genuine correct observation, yet insufficient here to turn a mechanical combination of known complete classifications into a new mathematical contribution. Reproducible finite verification is not a value substitute.
